title: SF3866 (2019-2020 Regular): Civilly committed sex offenders firearms possession prohibition; felony drive-by shooting clarification; criminal gang member firearm possession in public without a permit to carry penalties increase; noncitizen permit to carry firearm applicant background check information collection expansion

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (1st  Engrossment; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/91/2020/0/SF/3866/versions/1/)
provenance.note: 1st Engrossment (date blank in record), other. No vote in the record. Sections 1 to 3 and 5 amend protective-order and sentencing laws to point to the new section 624.7134 (gun removal). Section 10/11 expand the non-citizen permit application and add an immigration status check (not a deportation topic). Struck text is not quoted.

Section 8 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 2): When a person becomes ineligible to possess a firearm under a provision described in subdivision 1, the court shall order the person to transfer any firearms that the person possesses, within three business days, to a federally licensed firearms dealer, a law enforcement agency, or a third party who may lawfully receive them.
Section 9 (Minn. Stat. 624.714, subd. 1a): A member of a criminal gang, as defined in section 609.229, subdivision 1, who is convicted of violating this subdivision is guilty of a felony.
Section 4 (Minn. Stat. 609.66, subd. 1e): A person convicted under paragraph (a), clause (2) or (3), may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than ten years or to payment of a fine of not more than $20,000, or both.
